To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intra-amygdala administration of a specific GABAA ϕ receptor antagonist reduced anxiety in rats, whereas the intra-amygala administration of a GABAA ϵ receptor antagonist did not have any effect on anxiety.
GABAA receptor ρ subunits are expressed in the amygdala and their blockade by (1,2 5,6-tetrhydropyridin-4-yl)phosphonic acid, a selective antagonist, induces anxiolytic-like effects.
the intra-amygdala administration of the GABAR ρ antagonist, (1,2 5,6-tetrathydropyridine4-yl)methlyphosphinic acid reduces the exploration of the elevated plus maze without affecting locomotion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which GABAA ϕ subunits are expressed in the rat amygalda and its role in anxiety and fear.
the role of GABAergic neurotransmission in the amygdala in the control of anxiety and fear.
the role played by GABAA ϕ receptors in the modulation of the fear and anxiety induced by the intra-amygdala administration of bicuculline.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

GABAA receptors are present in the amygdala, and that the subunit composition of GABAA receptors is heterogeneous, and that the GABAA ρm receptor subtype has been identified in the rat basolateral amygdala, where it may be involved in the modulation of anxiety and fear.

the GABAA ϕ receptor antagonist, (1,2-5,6-tetrhydropyridin-4-yl) methylphosphinic acid (TPMPA), reduced the exploration of the elevated plus maze without altering locomotion, while the GABAA α receptor antagonist, bicucullin, induced seizures, but did not affect exploration.
the GABAA ϕ receptor may have a role on fear and anxiety, but the data are inconclusive and more research is needed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GABAA ϕ receptors are involved in fear and anxiety.

GABAA receptors in the amygdala may be involved in the regulation of anxiety and fear responses, and GABAA ϕ receptors may be more involved in the control of fear responses, whereas GABAA ϵ receptors may be involved in controlling both fear and anxiety.
GABAA receptors may play a role in the modulation by the amygdala of fear and anxiety and that this modulation is mediated by GABAA ρm receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amygdala may have a role as an anxiety generator, which may be modulated by GABAA ϕ receptors.
GABAAρ receptors may have a key role in the amygadala in the modulation of anxiety.
the GABA ρ receptor antagonist 1,2,4,5-THPMPA (6 pmol/s) decreased the exploration of the elevated plus maze without affecting locomotion.
